statement: The function returns a result r. Let I = {i | 0 <= i < len(weight)}. For a set S of indices, define sum(S) to be the sum of weight[i] over all i in S, with sum(empty) = 0. Then r is the maximum cardinality of a subset S of I such that sum(S) <= 5000. Equivalently: (1) there exists S subset of I with |S| = r and sum(S) <= 5000; and (2) for every T subset of I with sum(T) <= 5000, |T| <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(weight) <= 10^3 (1000), and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weight), 1 <= weight[i] <= 10^3 (1000).

preconditions: 1 <= len(weight) <= 10^3 (1000), and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weight), 1 <= weight[i] <= 10^3 (1000).

preconditions: 1 <= len(weight) <= 10^3 (1000), and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weight), 1 <= weight[i] <= 10^3 (1000).

statement: Whenever the call on weight returns r and the call on weight' returns r', we have r <= r' <= r + 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(weight) <= 10^3 (1000), for every i with 0 <= i < len(weight), 1 <= weight[i] <= 10^3 (1000); p is an integer with 1 <= p <= 1000; and len(weight) + 1 <= 1000. Let weight' be the slice with len(weight') = len(weight) + 1, weight'[i] = weight[i] for 0 <= i < len(weight), and weight'[len(weight)] = p.

statement: Whenever the call on weight returns r and the call on weight' returns r', we have r' <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(weight) <= 10^3 (1000), for every i with 0 <= i < len(weight), 1 <= weight[i] <= 10^3 (1000). Let weight' be another slice with the same length such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(weight), 1 <= weight'[i] <= 1000 and weight[i] <= weight'[i].

statement: Whenever the call on weight returns r and the call on weight' returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(weight) <= 10^3 (1000), and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weight), 1 <= weight[i] <= 10^3 (1000). Let weight' be another slice of the same length such that there is a bijection pi from {0,...,len(weight)-1} to itself with weight'[i] = weight[pi(i)] for every i.

statement: The function returns a result r. Let s be the list obtained by sorting the entries of weight in nondecreasing order, so len(s) = len(weight) and s has the same multiset of values as weight. Then the sum s[0] + ... + s[r-1] is at most 5000 (this sum is empty and equals 0 if r = 0), and if r < len(weight), then also s[0] + ... + s[r] is greater than 5000.
preconditions: 1 <= len(weight) <= 10^3 (1000), and for every i with 0 <= i < len(weight), 1 <= weight[i] <= 10^3 (1000).
